explanations: applyDeposit writes the two halves of one journal (the deposit debit and the copay credit) in two separate transactions. If the process crashes, the connection drops or the second write fails after the first commit, the ledger holds a one-sided entry: the deposit has been drawn down but the copay was never credited (and the next call would deduct from the deposit again). chargeNoShowFee shows the correct pattern, where both entries go through postJournal inside one tx.run so they commit or roll back together and the balance check runs before anything is written.

The guard on the charged flag happens inside the transaction, immediately before the entries are written, and the method returns early when it reports that the flag was already set. The status check is read-only and would pass for both, but it is not what protects against a double charge. multiplyExact is plain arithmetic with no locking.

Math.multiplyExact(2501, 2000) = 5,002,000, divided by 10,000 using long division = 500 (500.2 truncated). A long cannot hold a fractional cent, 501 would need rounding up, and 5,002 forgets the division by the 10,000 basis-point base.

markNoShowFeeCharged, both appends and the sum check all execute on the same Connection within one tx.run call, so an exception thrown by the second append propagates out of the body and the runner rolls the whole unit back. The other choices describe partial commits that this single-transaction structure is meant to rule out.
